paraphrase: Something changes, in the general sense of change: some thing changes in some characteristic, quality or relation, the thoughts of conscious beings included. Floor item F3 (#1007).

self_evident.note: Floor item F3 (#1007), approved by the owner on the observation basis; the approval plus that basis is the evidence, so no stating text is pinned (owner, 2026-11-05). Closest texts, recorded as supporting justifications: Aquinas, ST I q.2 a.3 (aliqua moveri, sensu constat) and Aristotle, Physics I.2, 185a12-14 (some natural things move, evident by induction). Both state motion, not change in this general sense: identifying motion or Aristotle's μεταβολή with McTaggart's 'change' is a reading step no source states (TruthCore.Alternatives.McTaggart). Recorded rival: McTaggart's 1908 bundle, defeated by consequence against F3 (MCTAGGART-BUNDLE-DEFEATED-BY-CHANGE); his later reply that appearers do not change is compatible with F3 and is not defeated. Parmenides' denial of change (fr. 8) is not recorded as a rival yet: it waits for a pinned witness.
